Make every player-visible string in your folders bilingual, with Hebrew written natively (docs/LOCALIZATION.md).
Where English text hides: JSX text; aria-label / title / placeholder / alt attributes; tutorial steps; nudges, hints, errors, empty states; toasts and bus payloads you emit (toast message, reward:granted label/value text, achievement:unlocked title/description) — choose the language with services.locale / ctx.locale at emit time; text drawn on canvas; constants arrays (quips, achievement lists, tips); HubEntry/HudWidget titles registered in install(services) (pick by services.locale); SceneModule-level text.
Pattern: a strings.ts per folder (or per sub-area if large) with defineStrings({ en, he }) from @core; components call useStrings(S) from @ui-kit; non-Preact code uses pickStrings(S, locale). Interpolations are functions. Keep English verbatim.
Then make the module look right in the Hebrew edition (RTL): logical CSS properties, directional icons flipped, clinical/spatial visuals stay dir="ltr", Latin/number runs wrapped so punctuation lands correctly, Hebrew fonts render. Verify with ?lang=he screenshots (desktop + 375px) and also confirm the English screen (no lang param) is unchanged.
YOUR SCOPE: the design system (component default labels like Close/Back, toast host, Screen chrome, tooltips, any built-in text), base RTL behaviour for the whole app: in ui-kit make directional icons (chevron-left/right, arrow-left/right) flip under [dir=rtl] via a class or CSS, check every component in RTL (Modal close position, Tabs order, ProgressBar fill direction, Tooltip placement, SpeechBubble tail, Screen top bar & back button — the back chevron must point right in RTL). The 5 game modes in src/modes/ (title, tagline via `text: { he }` on each ModeModule; locked() reasons via services.locale). src/render: any aria-labels/text in avatars, FX floatText defaults. Sandbox page to check: ?lang=he&sandbox=page/ui-kit.

Mini-game specifics: add `text: { he: { title, instructions, teaches } }` to each MiniGameModule (see miniGameText in @core); everything inside mount() uses ctx.locale. report() chart lines (RevealedFinding label/value) must be in the edition language too: give report access to the locale — report(findings, patient) has no locale parameter, so keep report() English-compatible and add an internal reportFor(findings, patient, locale) that mount() uses for the chart, OR read the locale from a module-level setter set in mount(); choose the cleanest option and keep report()'s English output byte-identical for existing tests. Optotypes (Snellen/ETDRS letters, tumbling E) stay Latin as on Israeli charts; the patient still reads letter names. Clinical abbreviations (OD/OS, RAPD, IOP, mmHg, D, Δ, C/D) stay as Israeli optometrists use them. Spatial instrument views must never mirror.
YOUR SCOPE: visual acuity + pinhole, phoropter ('אחת או שתיים?' — the classic patient dialogue in natural Hebrew), retinoscopy. Check ?lang=he&sandbox=minigame/<id> for each (pinhole: ?lang=he&sandbox=minigame/pinhole).

Write Hebrew content OVERLAYS (pure data) — the clinical data stays single-sourced in the English files, you rewrite only the words.
Read each English case/diagnosis fully, understand the clinical story and the patient as a person, then write the Hebrew as an Israeli clinician-writer would, from scratch (docs/LOCALIZATION.md §1-2). Adapt the patient to Israel where natural (name, occupation, places, cultural references, the way they talk), consistent with their age, sex and avatar (skin tone) and keeping every clinical fact, number, timeline and risk factor identical. Patients speak in their own gendered voice. History questions are what an Israeli optometrist would actually ask, in the plural-free direct form addressed to the patient (e.g. "מתי זה התחיל?", "יש כאב בתנועות העיניים?"). Teaching points, management and red flags: precise Israeli professional Hebrew with the terminology table.
Validate: npx vitest run tests/content-he.test.ts tests/content.test.ts and npm run check:mod -- <your folder>. Also open a case in the Hebrew edition to read it in context: node scripts/shot.cjs "?lang=he&sandbox=scene/exam&caseId=<id>" /tmp/shots/he-<id>.png.
YOUR SCOPE: Hebrew overlays for ALL 57 diagnoses: src/content/he/diagnoses/<category>.ts, each `export default DiagnosisText[]` (type from @core) mirroring the English files in src/content/diagnoses/. name (the Hebrew clinical name Israelis use, e.g. 'סגירת זווית חריפה', with the English/Latin name in aka if clinicians use it), aka, summary, keyFindings, pearls — the codex an Israeli student would love to study from.
